speaker: Doctor

The hematocrit of 51% is within the normal range for a newborn, suggesting hemolysis is not the primary cause of this jaundice. Have you noticed the baby becoming lethargic or difficult to wake up, and did you notice the urine is very dark?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The Coombs test and blood smear results appear normal, which makes immune-mediated hemolysis less likely. Given the significant unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia (16.1 mg/dL) in an otherwise stable newborn, has the baby had any blood transfusions recently, and is the mother's blood type known?
